The appellant / State of Madhya Pradesh through the Collector has filed the present appeal under Section 2(1) of the Madhya Pradesh Uchcha Nyayalaya (Khand Nyay Peeth to Appeal) Adhiniyam,

sentences.text: The facts of the case reveal that respondent No.1 / writ petitioner is a partnership Firm engaged in the business of sale of petroleum products through an outlet known as 'M/s Laxmi Service Station' situated at A.B. Road, G.P.O. Square, Indore.
The writ petitioner has a license issued by Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL) to sell petroleum products.
Initially, the said license was given to M/s Standard Vacuum Oil Company.
Before commissioning the outlet, No Objection Certificate was issued by the then District Authority under the provisions of the Petroleum Act, 1934 to the erstwhile owner.
Thereafter, HPCL took the control of the said outlet and allotted it to respondent No.1.
The respondent Firm is continuously operating the retail outlet by virtue of the agreement of the dealership with HPCL.
Currently, the lease agreement dated 12.05.2006 is valid for a period of 30 years.
03. On 02.05.2022, an accident of fire took place while unloading the petroleum product at Laxmi Service Station at Indore by the tankers of HPCL.

The incident was reported to the HPCL Officials,
who conducted the inspection and submitted the report to the head office.
The District Food Officer also carried out the inspection and took the samples and nothing wrong was found.

04. The Additional District Magistrate, Indore suo moto took cognizance of the above accident and issued a show-cause notice to the Regional Manager and Assistant Manager (Sales) of HPCL on 03.05.2022 and sought an explanation within three days.

The Regional Manager and Assistant Manager (Sales) replied that the erring driver and helper of the tanker truck have been removed from employment and based on the recommendation of the Three Members' Committee, detailed guidelines have been issued to the writ petitioner.

05. The District Magistrate, Indore issued a show-cause notice on 17.05.2022 to the writ petitioner as to why the No Objection Certificate issued under Rule 115(3) of the Petroleum Rules be not recalled.
The writ petitioner / Firm submitted a reply explaining the action taken by the writ petitioner against its employees.

Vide impugned order dated 14.07.2022 the learned District Magistrate has cancelled the No Objection Certificate in exercise of the power conferred under Rule 150 of the Petroleum Rules, 2002 and further directed the Chief Explosive Controller, Bhopal for initiation of proceedings in relation to cancellation of the license.

The District Magistrate has also directed the Commissioner, Municipal Corporation, Indore for taking action with respect to the The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs M/S Laxmi Service Station on 21 September, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84209663/
2 business license.

sentences.text: Being aggrieved by the aforesaid action, the writ petitioner filed a writ petition before the Writ Court challenging the authority of the District Magistrate of taking impugned action under the provisions of the Petroleum Act & Petroleum Rules.

The Writ Court has held that in the city of Indore, the Commissioner of Police System has been introduced vide notification dated 09.12.2021 and as per the definition under Rule 2(x) of the Petroleum Rules, 2002, the District Authority means the Commissioner of Police or Deputy Commissioner of Police, therefore, the District Magistrate has no power to cancel the No Objection Certificate under Rule 150 of the Petroleum Rules.

The Writ Court has negatived the contention of the Government Advocate that petroleum is not included in the Schedule appended to the notification dated 09.12.2021 issued by the Home Department establishing the Police Commissioner System in the city of Indore.
The Writ Court vide order dated 08.09.2022 has allowed the writ petition and quashed the order cancelling the No Objection Certificate.
Hence, the present writ appeal is before this Court.

07. We have heard Shri Aditya Garg, learned Government Advocate for the appellant / State, Shri Piyush Mathur, learned Senior Counsel for respondent No.1 / writ petitioner and Shri Aniket Naik,
learned counsel for respondent No.4 and perused the record.
08. The only issue which requires our consideration is whether the District Magistrate, Indore has rightly exercised its authority under Rule 150 of the Petroleum Rules or not?

09. The District Authority is defined under Rule 2(x) of the Petroleum Rules, according to which in towns having a Commissioner of Police, the Commissioner / Deputy Commissioner; in other places,
the District Magistrate.
Admittedly vide notification dated 09.12.2022, the Commissioner of Police System has been established in the city of Indore, therefore, the District Authority means Commissioner of Police.
Hence, the power of the District Magistrate ceases the moment the Commissioner of Police System has been established.

10. Shri Aditya Garg, learned Government Advocate emphasized on the list of statutes mention in Schedule appended to the aforesaid notification in which only 9 enactments are there in which the function of District Magistrate has been directed to be discharged by the Commissioner of Police,
Indore including sub- section (5) of Section 20 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

According to Shri Garg, learned Government Advocate, the Petroleum Act & Rules have not been included in the Schedule, therefore, the power of the District Magistrate continues to be exercised under the Petroleum Act & Rules.

The said contention is not acceptable because there is no need to include the Petroleum Act & Rules in the Schedule of the aforesaid notification when Rule 2(x) of the Petroleum Rules specifically provides that in a town having a Commissioner of Police, the Commissioner or Deputy Commissioner of Police shall be a District Authority and any other place the District Magistrate shall be a District Authority, therefore, there is no need to include the enactment of Petroleum Act & Rules in the Schedule for giving the power from District Magistrate to Commissioner.
Hence, the District Magistrate has wrongly exercised the power and without authority under the Petroleum Act and Rules, the Writ Court has rightly set aside the impugned order.

sentences.text: Though this ground has not been raised by the petitioner in the Writ Petition, but the District Authority under Rule 144(4), the licensing authority i.e. Chief Controller or the Controller, as the case may be, on an application for a new license with the site plan showing the location of the premises is to examine only that, there is no objection only in respect of the location of the site.

Likewise, under Rule 150, the No Objection Certificate is liable to be cancelled if the District Authority of the State Government, as the case may be, is satisfied that the licensee has ceased to have any right to use the site for storing the petroleum product.

Rule 150 of the Petroleum Rules is reproduced below:-
"150. Cancellation of no-objection certificate.--

( 1 ) A no-objection certificate granted under rule 144 shall be liable to be cancelled by the District Authority or the State Government, if the District Authority or the State Government is satisfied, that the licensee has ceased to have any right to use the site for storing petroleum:
Provided that before cancelling a no-objection certificate, the licensee shall be given a reasonable opportunity of being heard.

(2) A District Authority or a State Government cancelling a no-objection certificate shall record, in writing, the reasons for such cancellation and shall immediately furnish to the licensee and to the licensing authority concerned, copy of the order cancelling the no-objection certificate.
[Emphasis Supplied]
12. As per sub rule (1) of Rule 150, a No Objection Certificate granted under Rule 144 in respect of the location of the site shall be liable to be cancelled by the District Authority or by the State Government, if the licensee ceased to have any right to use the site for storing the petroleum.
It is not a case of the District Authority that the writ petitioner has lost the right to use the site.

Hence,
for the grant of the No Objection Certificate and cancellation of the No Objection Certificate, the District Authority is having the right to examine the location and rights of the parties on a site.
We do not find any reason to interfere with the order passed by Writ Court.
In view of the above, Writ Appeal stands dismissed.

(VIVEK RUSIA) (AMAR NATH (KESHARWANI))
